{
  "format": 1,
  "rule": "req~inspector.debug-only~1",
  "example": "a debug build with and without the flag",
  "files": {},
  "steps": [
    {"line": "* When a debug build of palantir launches without the inspector launch flag",
     "do": [{"launch": {"build": "debug", "inspector": false}, "as": "bare"}],
     "expect": []},
    {"line": "* Then it creates no inspector socket",
     "do": [{"sleep": 2},
            {"inspect": ["list"], "exit": "any", "as": "listed"},
            {"inspect": ["state"], "exit": "any", "as": "probe"}],
     "expect": [{"that": ".bare.pid as $p | (.listed.exit == 0 or .listed.exit == 2) and ((.listed.sockets // []) | all((.pid | tostring) != ($p | tostring)))",
                 "why": "no inspector socket is listed for the palantir launched without the flag"},
                {"that": ".probe.exit == 2",
                 "why": "palantir-inspect finds no socket to reach that palantir"}]},
    {"line": "* When it launches again with the flag",
     "do": [{"quit": true},
            {"launch": {"build": "debug", "inspector": true}, "as": "flagged"}],
     "expect": []},
    {"line": "* Then it answers on a socket in a directory only the user can open",
     "do": [{"inspect": ["wait"], "exit": "any", "as": "settled"},
            {"inspect": ["list"], "exit": "any", "as": "listening"},
            {"inspect": ["state"], "exit": "any", "as": "answer"},
            {"stat": {"jq": "first(.flagged.pid as $p | .listening.sockets[]? | select((.pid | tostring) == ($p | tostring)) | .path) // \"\""}, "as": "socket"},
            {"stat": {"jq": "(first(.flagged.pid as $p | .listening.sockets[]? | select((.pid | tostring) == ($p | tostring)) | .path) // \"\") | split(\"/\") | .[:-1] | join(\"/\")"}, "as": "folder"}],
     "expect": [{"that": ".answer.exit == 0 and (.answer.json | type) == \"object\"",
                 "why": "the inspector answers a state request from the palantir launched with the flag"},
                {"that": ".flagged.pid as $p | .listening.exit == 0 and any(.listening.sockets[]?; (.pid | tostring) == ($p | tostring))",
                 "why": "that palantir is listed as listening on a socket"},
                {"that": ".socket.exists and (.socket.isDirectory | not)",
                 "why": "the socket it listens on is on disk at the listed path"},
                {"that": ".folder.exists and .folder.isDirectory",
                 "why": "the socket's folder is a real directory, not a symlink"},
                {"that": "(.folder.uid | tostring) == (.uid | tostring)",
                 "why": "the user owns the socket's directory"},
                {"that": ".folder.mode | .[-3:] | (.[1:] == \"00\") and ((.[0:1] | tonumber) as $o | $o == 5 or $o == 7)",
                 "why": "the directory grants group and others nothing and lets its owner list and enter it"}]}
  ]
}
EOF

cat > work/answer.md <<'EOF'
- Left as is: "Then it creates no inspector socket": `inspect ["list"]` and `.probe.exit == 2`: the review is right that these only see a socket that listens, and that this is a limit of the tools. `list` shows only palantirs that are listening. `stat` needs a path known in advance, and the socket's path is only learned from the flagged launch in a later step. So the check asserts the most that can be observed: nothing listed for that pid, and `state` cannot reach it.
- Fixed: the ancestor walk stopping at level 63: the walk now goes up through level 339 (up0..up339, `range(0; 340)`). That is every level a stat path can reach: macOS caps paths at 1023 bytes, and the shortest socket folder with ancestors (`/a`) plus `/.` and 339 `/..` is 1021 bytes. A level whose path would be longer stats `/.` (the root, an ancestor of every path) instead. A guarding folder deeper than any path can reach is beyond what the tools can see.
- Left as is: the mode/uid permission expectation and ACLs: the review is right, and it is a limit of the tools. `stat` returns only exists, mode, uid and isDirectory. No documented tool reads ACLs, and no tool reads the group id either, so the check also cannot tell a group that contains only the user from a shared group like staff. The check reads the mode bits as written and never loosens them.
EOF
